dial.summary: July's shock −23,000 NFP print (first monthly job loss in years, vs +80k consensus) slashed September rate-hike odds from 58% to 30%, compressing real yields from 2.40% to 2.37% and keeping DXY neutral at 99.75 — six of eight macro indicators remain supportive, with ISM Manufacturing holding at a 4-year high of 55.6%, stablecoin dominance declining further to 13.3%, and BTC dominance rising to 56.8% (TOTAL crypto $2.28T); real yields at 2.37% are the lone structural headwind but the NFP miss puts the compression path squarely in focus ahead of July CPI (Aug 12) and FOMC Minutes (Aug 19).

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $102,663.81B ($102.66T) for June 2026 — July 2026 global aggregate not yet published on MacroMicro as of August 8; US M2 (H.6 weekly) rose to $23.3T in July 2026 (up from $23.16T in June, +$0.14T, 29th consecutive monthly increase, +5.6% YoY), confirming continued global liquidity expansion; estimated global aggregate ~$103.0–103.3T as July central bank data is incorporated across all four banks; prior run's $103.2T estimate maintained pending official MacroMicro July publication; 4-week trend up: ~$102.5T (early July estimate) → ~$103.2T (Aug 8 estimate) — above the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY growth remains positive; headwind condition — contracting YoY — not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3, 2026) remains the most recent reading — 2.3pp above June's 53.3%, highest since May 2022, seventh consecutive expansion month; August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI does not release until September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: Production 58.5%, New Orders 56.7%, Employment 52.8% (first factory expansion in 33 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; July NFP released August 7 at −23,000 (first monthly job loss in years, vs +80k consensus) — a sharp deterioration that reduces the probability of any September rate hike from 58% to 30%, shifting the macro backdrop more dovish despite the ISM strength; 4-week trend up: 53.3% (June) → 55.6% (July) = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.75 on August 8, 2026 (daily range 99.68–99.74); DXY fell from 99.93 (August 7 pre-NFP) following the −23,000 July NFP miss which drove the US 10-year yield down ~7bps to ~4.60% and the 2-year down ~5bps to ~4.19%, reducing the dollar's yield advantage; 30-day trend: DXY ~100.9 (July 14 confirmed) and ~101.3 (July 1 per prior data) → 99.75 (Aug 8) — a decline of ~1.2–1.6%, above the 0.5% flat threshold; trend down; status NEUTRAL per ICE DXY spot threshold (99.75 is above the 97.5 supportive boundary but below the 100 headwind boundary); July CPI (Aug 12) is the primary directional catalyst — a sub-3% print would accelerate DXY toward 97.5 (supportive), a hot print could temporarily restore DXY above 100 (headwind) despite the labor market deterioration.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield) at approximately 2.37% as of August 7–8, 2026 — down from the August 4 reading of 2.40% as the July NFP shock (−23,000, first monthly job loss in years) drove nominal 10-year yields down ~7bps to ~4.60% with a modest real-yield compression effect; 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (July 7 estimate) → 2.37% (Aug 7) = +19bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold — the lone remaining structural headwind; September FOMC hike probability dropped from 58% to 30%, shifting the forward path toward neutral-to-easing; July CPI (Aug 12) is the primary real-yield compression catalyst — a soft print combined with continued labor softening could bring DFII10 below 2.0%, flipping status to neutral).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 7, 2026 post-NFP close: DGS10 ~4.60% (fell ~7bps on −23,000 July NFP miss), DGS2 ~4.19% (fell ~5bps), spread ~+0.41% (+41bps); 4-week comparison: July 7 spread ~+0.35% (+35bps) → Aug 7 ~+0.41% (+41bps) = +6bps steepening, just above the 5bps flat threshold — trend up; status remains SUPPORTIVE (curve is positive at +41bps AND steepening on a 4-week basis); the NFP-driven 2Y decline (rate-cut repricing) steepens the curve as short rates are repriced lower faster than long rates; July CPI (Aug 12) and FOMC Minutes (Aug 19) are the next curve catalysts — a soft CPI would compress the 2Y further and deepen steepening; Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29) is the subsequent major catalyst.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL (H.4.1): $6,741B ($6.74T) confirmed for week ending July 29, 2026 (H.4.1 dated July 30, released July 31) — down $9B from week ending July 22 ($6,750B per convextrade.com tracker); August 5 weekly data (released in H.4.1 dated August 7) not yet indexed by web sources as of August 8; prior run estimate of $6,749B for Aug 5 maintained as the most-recent official figure is July 29 at $6,741B (within $8B); 4-week trend flat: ~$6,720B (July 8 estimate) → $6,741B (July 29 confirmed) = +$21B (+0.31%), within the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (balance sheet holding at post-2022 plateau; ~$95B above one year ago; no aggressive QT with rising overnight rates; July 29 FOMC held at 3.50–3.75%, 9-3 vote; next H.4.1 covering Aug 12 data releases August 13).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: Live funding rate data inaccessible — CoinGlass returned network-blocked error; value carried forward at +0.004%/8h; contextual signals as of August 8, 2026: BTC dominance 56.8% (up from 56.58%), BTC market cap $1.29T, total crypto market cap $2.28T; July NFP shock (−23,000, first monthly job loss in years) reduced September rate-hike probability from 58% to 30%, a macro backdrop consistent with spot accumulation rather than leveraged long speculation; near-zero positive funding well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June toward near-zero); status supportive (near-zero funding signals healthy long bias without leverage overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$302B (USDT ~$186B, USDC ~$75B, balance in USDS/DAI/PYUSD) as of August 8, 2026; total crypto market cap $2.28T; stablecoin dominance $302B / $2.28T ≈ 13.28% — essentially flat day-over-day from yesterday's 13.3% as stablecoin issuance kept pace with TOTAL crypto; 30-day trend down: July 8 dominance ~14.3% → Aug 8 ~13.3% = −1.0pp compression as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets over 30 days; status supportive (falling on 30-day basis; headwind threshold requires rising dominance WHILE TOTAL crypto is also rising — not met since dominance fell net over 30 days as TOTAL rose from ~$2.10T to $2.28T); BTC dominance at 56.8% confirms capital inflow has favored BTC over alts.

upcoming.title: Reserve Bank of Australia Rate Decision (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision at 14:30 AEST — first major central bank decision of the week; now arrives with a dramatically shifted global backdrop after July US NFP printed −23,000 (first monthly job loss in years, vs +80k consensus) on August 7; BOE held at 3.75% (July 30 decision); Fed held at 3.50–3.75% (July 29, 9-3 vote); RBA decision shapes commodity currency (AUD/USD) outlook and provides a global-rate-cycle read-through; a hold or dovish tilt would reinforce expectations of global monetary easing, supportive for risk assets ahead of the critical July CPI print on August 12.

upcoming.title: CPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — the most critical data point of the week, arriving one trading day after July NFP's shock −23,000 print (first job loss in years); real yields at 2.37% (headwind) and DXY at 99.75 (neutral band) make a soft CPI the primary catalyst for real-yield compression and a potential DXY break below 97.5 (which would flip DXY to supportive); ISM Prices Paid elevated in both Manufacturing (71.1%) and Services (both above 70), signaling pipeline pressure; however oil-price moderation on Iran diplomatic progress provides a deflationary offset in the energy component; a soft July CPI (headline <2.8%, core <3.0%) would accelerate the September rate-cut debate already energized by the NFP miss; a hot print would complicate the easing path despite the labor deterioration and is the principal near-term risk to the BTC Accumulation thesis.

upcoming.title: PPI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released one day after July CPI (August 12); PPI feeds directly into core PCE components (healthcare and financial services); ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid at 71.1% signals upstream pipeline pressure, but oil-price moderation may provide a significant goods PPI offset; arriving the day after CPI in the context of the July NFP shock (−23,000), a soft PPI would reinforce the disinflation + labor-softening combination that strengthens the September rate-cut case; a hot PPI — particularly in trade services or healthcare — would signal pipeline risks not captured in headline CPI, complicating September cut pricing even with the labor market deteriorating.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 8, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ending August 8, 2026 — the first weekly labor read following July NFP's shock −23,000 print (August 7); prior weeks showed low claims (~197–225k); if claims begin rising here, it would corroborate the NFP deterioration and significantly increase September rate-cut probability beyond the already-repriced 70% hold / 30% hike distribution; ISM Services Employment contracted to 47.4% in July (first contraction since June 2024), adding a pre-existing bearish signal; released alongside July PPI — a claims + PPI surprise combination in either direction amplifies the market reaction.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (July 2026)
upcoming.note: US Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — the key growth gauge of the week, arriving after the NFP shock (−23,000, Aug 7), CPI (Aug 12), and PPI (Aug 13); a miss in retail sales on top of the labor deterioration would compound the soft-landing → hard-landing concern; June 2026 retail sales rose 0.2% MoM, +6.7% YoY; ISM Manufacturing Production (58.5%) and New Orders (56.7%) suggest demand-side support, but the employment collapse may weigh on August spending; a strong retail print (>0.4% MoM) would confirm consumer resilience despite the labor miss and reinforce BTC Accumulation; a weak print would deepen September rate-cut expectations and put pressure on real yields from 2.37%.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (August 2026 preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment preliminary reading for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — the first sentiment read post July NFP (−23,000, Aug 7) and post July CPI (Aug 12); July 2026 UMich came in at 54.4 (highest since February 2026); the August preliminary captures the immediate consumer reaction to the job loss data and any inflation repricing; the 5-year inflation expectation component is particularly watched given ISM Prices Paid elevated in both Manufacturing (71.1%) and Services; oil-price moderation could reduce 1-year inflation expectations and lift headline sentiment; a sentiment drop alongside a negative NFP would compound recession-risk signals, while a resilient reading would support the soft-landing narrative.
